references.text: The same theme of holiness: Israel's people are to consecrate themselves because the Lord is holy and sanctifies them. The expression 'אֲנִי יְהוָה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם' (I am the Lord who sanctifies you) appears in both texts.
Parallel context regarding the priests' holiness and their role in presenting 'לֶחֶם אֱלֹהֵיהֶם' (their God's bread/food).
The same chapter that mentions 'לֶחֶם אֱלֹהָיו' (his God's bread) in connection with priestly service.
Repeats the formula 'אֲנִי יְהוָה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם' (I am the Lord who sanctifies you) and the command not to profane God's holy name.
The fundamental command of holiness: 'קְדֹשִׁים תִּהְיוּ כִּי קָדוֹשׁ אֲנִי יְהוָה' (you shall be holy, for I the Lord your God am holy).
The Lord identifies himself as 'יְהוָה מְקַדִּשְׁכֶם' (the Lord who sanctifies you) in connection with the Sabbath command.
The offering is described as 'לֶחֶם אִשֶּׁה לַיהוָה' (a food offering by fire to the Lord), the same concept of 'God's bread'.
Peter quotes the holiness command from Leviticus: 'ἅγιοι ἔσεσθε, ὅτι ἐγὼ ἅγιος' (you shall be holy, for I am holy).
Jesus as 'ὁ ἁγιάζων' (the one who sanctifies) and believers as 'οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι' (those being sanctified) – parallel to God sanctifying his people.
The priests are to teach the people the difference between holy and common, parallel to the priests' role in maintaining holiness.
